scope: Optional private proxy ownership persistence: source backend, actual local Docker daemon, graceful/forced proxy restart and cleanup-only recovery. No actual VM/private-container mount or installed app deployment.

reproduced_before_fix.cause: The previous proxy lost ownership after restart; configured restart acceptance could not recover a trusted cleanup-only receipt.

implementation: A separate proxy-private SQLite ledger records full owned IDs, generated names, mount-source references and retirement state. It is deliberately outside application-writable state and supplied only to the proxy.

Private service ownership/permissions, canonical paths, no file links, daemon/project binding, receipt validation and an exclusive SQLite writer lock establish the storage trust boundary. No account login or identity service was added.

SQLite EXTRA synchronization and atomic updates commit receipts before create acknowledgments. A write failure preserves memory/last-commit evidence and fences new creation/execution while known-ID cleanup remains possible.
Every restored ID is cleanup-only. Inspect and deletion are permitted; attach/start/wait/kill/resize remain blocked. No stored task body, command, credential value or executable queue is replayed.

Each forwarded connection probes daemon identity and reuses that same keep-alive connection for the authorized request. The current project is checked from the same policy snapshot used for authorization.

The optional Compose override mounts private state only into the proxy, requires a precreated host directory, and adds the stdlib-only state helper. Deployments without the override retain memory-only behavior.
verified: Actual graceful proxy restart and SIGKILL preserve committed cleanup authority; the old stopped container is never started and is removed only by explicit recovery.
Configured failed-removal and reused-name drills retain the prior safety boundaries.
Memory-only restart remains unconfirmed. Enabling a fresh ledger leaves preexisting unrecorded containers untouched and requires manual review.
Changed daemon/project binding, damaged/future receipts, corrupt database, unsafe modes, symlinks/hard links and concurrent owners are rejected in the required gate.
Exclusive writer ownership persists through commits and releases when the proxy exits; actual forced-termination restart succeeds.
Identity framing consumes exactly one bounded length/chunked response, leaving the same stream ready for the next request. Invalid/unbounded/unresponsive probes fail without retry.
Recovered grants and storage-error grants cannot execute old/uncommitted containers. Ordinary new receipts retain their normal in-process permissions.
The persistence module runs with Nexus imports disabled; the optional Compose service override grants no mount to Studio.
All disposable analysis containers and temporary proxy directories are gone; the unrelated llm-cli-proxy service remains running.

trust_boundary.protects_against: Application-controlled workspace/restore data cannot manufacture proxy receipts when the dedicated state directory remains outside all writable Studio mounts.
trust_boundary.trusted: Service owner and host/Docker administrators. Directory isolation and service ownership authenticate this operational inventory; it is not a cryptographic defense against a host administrator.
trust_boundary.binding: SHA-256 of daemon identity and the existing Nexus project key.

migration.opt_in: PROXY_STATE_DIR plus docker-compose.studio-proxy-state.yml; precreate an owned canonical private directory outside every writable Studio/credential mount.
migration.upgrade: Stop proxy-backed work and deploy matching launcher/policy/state files. Enabling persistence starts with no adopted legacy grants.
migration.backup_restore: Back up private ledger separately with the proxy stopped; preserve permissions and restore only to the same daemon/project.
migration.rollback: Stop work and remove optional override while retaining ledger unchanged. Memory-only rollback cannot restore its grants; rollback-era work remains unrecorded on re-enablement.
migration.uncertain_creates: A crash before receipt commit, record eviction or lost private state can require independent review. No unknown object is adopted by name or treated as absent.

quality.ruff: Changed files pass with the existing legacy Denied exception naming rule N818 excluded; no new lint exception was introduced.

pending: Actual private mount isolation, ownership mapping and filesystem behavior on the personal Linux VM/container deployment.
Actual Docker daemon restart, remote/SSH disconnect and power-loss/host storage acceptance. Wrong binding and failed-write fixtures are not certification of these environments.
Uncommitted, evicted and unrecorded legacy creates remain an explicit manual-review outcome.
Escaped MCP descendants, physical voice devices, selected live provider accounts and native/frozen/installed OS acceptance remain open.
The previously documented mount-source swap race is unchanged; host administrators remain trusted.
release_note: Recorded checksum manifest retained. Previous absent DMGs were not recreated or reverified.
